To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) SEARCHBreast is an online resource that facilitates sharing and re-use of breast cancer animal model material; (b) the resource is freely available; (c) it will help researchers to find and share surplus archival breast cancer animal material and (d) will help researchers to reduce their usage of animal models.
we have developed and made available a searchable database for sharing archival material from animal models of breast cancers.
we developed and launched an online database that allows researchers to share archival tissue from animal models of breast cancers, which is an underutilized resource.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification and development of new resources for breast cancer research, which will facilitate the implementation of the 3Rs and promote the use of human breast tissue models as replacements for animal models in breast research.

the identification, localisation and sharing of archival material from breast animal models, and will contribute to the development of a sustainable, coordinated and collaborative system for the sharing of animal material, with a view to reducing the number of animals used for research.
the 3Rs of animal experimentation—Replacement, Reduction, and Refinement.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SEARCHBreast will facilitate the 3Rs of animal welfare, by reducing the need for animal experimentation and increasing the use of existing resources, thereby reducing the number of animals used.
SEARCHBreast is an important new resource that has the potential to facilitate and accelerate breast cancer research and reduce reliance on animal models.
SEARCHBreast will help to reduce animal usage by facilitating the sharing of archival material and by promoting the use of replacement models.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SEARCHBreast database is the first of its kind and has the potential to be a game changer in breast cancer research by reducing animal usage.
we have developed a resource that will help researchers find and share surplus archival breast cancer tissue and will promote the use of human breast models in research.
SEARCHBreast is an initiative to facilitate the sharing and reuse of archival animal tissue, with the ultimate goal of reducing the use of animals in research.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a coordinated effort to share surplus animal material can reduce animal usage, and that this is best achieved by the establishment of a searchable resource that is freely available to the research community.
the 3Rs can be implemented by sharing and reusing existing resources, and that this approach is more effective than developing new ones.

we have developed a resource which will facilitate the sharing and re-use of animal material in breast cancer research, thereby reducing the need for new animal experiments and ultimately helping to address the 3R principles of replacement, reduction and refinement.
